title: Progressive Unblocking: Blocker Classification, Continuation Protocol, and Resume Format
body:
Blockers are normal. The wrong response to a blocker is to halt all work and wait. The right response is to classify the blocker precisely, identify its exact scope of impact, continue all unaffected work, produce maximum useful partial output, and create a resume point specific enough for a new agent to pick up without re-reading the prior conversation. An agent that produces nothing because one part of the task is blocked has failed. An agent that produces partial output with a clear resume point has succeeded.

**Blocker Classification Taxonomy (B1-B9):**

**B1 — Missing User Decision:** The task requires a choice that only the user can make. Context does not support an inference. The two options produce meaningfully different outputs. Resolution: ask the minimum question, state the default, document the blocker, continue all unblocked work. Do not classify as B1 when the decision is inferable from context — infer it and log it as a Type 2 flag.

**B2 — Missing Repo Context:** A referenced artifact, guide, or resource does not exist in the repository. Resolution: search thoroughly before classifying; create a placeholder if appropriate; continue with best available context; add guide-gap-check to recommended next actions. Do not halt work for a B2.

**B3 — Missing Guide:** No guide exists for the domain or topic. Resolution: document the gap with specificity; proceed without the guide, noting every assumption made; flag sections where accuracy is most dependent on the missing guide. B3 does not block work — it degrades confidence in accuracy, which must be communicated to the reviewer.

**B4 — Missing Source Material:** The task requires specific source material that was not provided and has no available substitute. Resolution: draft a structure-only or placeholder version of the affected section; label the placeholder explicitly; complete all sections not dependent on the missing source. Never fabricate source material.

**B5 — Failed Toolchain:** A tool, MCP server, file system operation, or external service has failed. Resolution: attempt the operation once; if it fails, do not retry in a loop; log the error with full context; identify whether a fallback method exists; use the fallback and document it; do not silently recover.

**B6 — Artifact Export Failure:** A completed document cannot be exported to the required format. Resolution: deliver the document in the closest available format (typically structured markdown); log the export failure with the exact error; note that the delivered format is a fallback. The content is complete; the format is not — this distinction must be explicit.

**B7 — Schema Conflict:** Two outputs conform to different versions of the same schema and cannot be merged without resolving the conflict. Resolution: identify the canonical schema version for this run; flag the conflict; if the non-canonical version can be mapped without data loss, do so and document the mapping; if data loss would occur, escalate before proceeding. Never silently merge outputs conforming to different schema versions.

**B8 — Canon Conflict:** Requested content contradicts an established canon record. Resolution: surface the conflict with specific citations (draft claim and canon record with path); do not silently override canon in either direction; escalate to the lead-editor or user. B8 is a hard stop for the conflicting content — all other sections may proceed.

**B9 — Validation Failure:** An output has failed a defined quality gate or schema validation check. Resolution: return to the failed stage; produce a specific issue list of which criteria failed and exactly what must change; do not attempt to 'partially advance' — gates are binary.

**Progressive Continuation Protocol:** (1) Classify the blocker using B1-B9. (2) Record it in the run cache or produce a blocker_report. (3) Determine impacted scope — specifically and only that work. (4) Identify all unimpacted work. (5) Continue all unimpacted work. (6) Produce maximum useful partial output. (7) Write a RESUME section specific enough for handoff.

**RESUME Section Requirements:** Blocked on (specific item); blocker classification; to resume (exact action required with options if enumerable); default if no response; when unblocked — first step (exact first action after resolution); already complete (enumerate finished deliverables with file paths); estimated remaining work. A RESUME section that says 'continue when ready' is not valid.
